phase: initial independent judgment (pre-validation); no tests/TLC executed; no code/spec edited
update_summary: etcd-raft adjacent update introducing the confchange package and ConfChangeV2 / joint consensus: tracker.Config gains Voters[1] (outgoing), LearnersNext and AutoLeave; applyConfChange is rebuilt on confchange.Changer (Simple / EnterJoint / LeaveJoint) with changed simple semantics (voter->learner demotion, no-op removal of unknown ids, rejection (panic) of zero-incoming-voter results and of >1 voter delta); leaders auto-propose an empty ConfChangeV2 (LeaveJoint) from raft.advance; maybeCommit after every applied conf change; quorum, vote, check-quorum and read-index decisions use joint quorums; node.run is rebuilt on RawNode (acceptReady/commitReady/raft.advance); RawNode.Ready becomes read-only; NewRawNode drops peers (Bootstrap replaces it); StartNode panics with zero peers; Status gains Config.

overall.reason: Most old safety contracts still state the right requirement and are kept verbatim (19). Ten must change: four because the requirement itself changed (configuration-effect function, Advance may now append a raft-generated LeaveJoint entry, joint quorums for elections/commits and for read confirmation) and six because they are written over the old {voters, learners} configuration and V1-only entry kinds, so they cannot express joint configurations or V2 entries. Four properties are added: the documented pendingConfIndex coverage invariant, configuration well-formedness (confchange.checkInvariants plus no zero-voter configs), applicability of raft-generated configuration entries, and a decision-time auto-leave initiation contract. No property is removed or weakened to match the new implementation. At least three new-source behaviours violate requirements that are kept: the Hup pending-config scan ignores V2 entries, auto-leave does not cover its entry with pendingConfIndex, and restore/InitialState drop the joint half of a ConfState. These must stay visible.

shared_definitions.note: Proposed representation shared by all modified/added predicates. Configuration mirrors tracker.Config (new/source/tracker/tracker.go:25-75): in=Voters[0], out=Voters[1], learners, next=LearnersNext, autoLeave. Entries keep V1 kinds with a single target; ConfChangeV2 entries use kind "ConfV2" with fields changes (Seq of [op \in V1Kinds, target]) and transition. Every entry record carries target, changes, transition (unused fields default to 0 / <<>> / "Auto"). ConfStep2 is an independent re-statement of confchange.go:49-181 + raftpb/confchange.go:96-105, not a copy of the model's ApplyConfCore; it returns ok=FALSE where the source returns an error (and raft.go:1454-1457 panics).
tla: EmptyCfg == [in |-> {}, out |-> {}, learners |-> {}, next |-> {}, autoLeave |-> FALSE]
CfgMembers(c) == c.in \cup c.out \cup c.learners   \* = DOMAIN prs (next \subseteq out)
Changes(e) == IF e.kind \in V1Kinds THEN <<[op |-> e.kind, target |-> e.target]>> ELSE e.changes
IsBootstrapEntry(e) == e.id=0 /\ e.kind="AddVoter" /\ e.term=1 /\ e.index \in 1..Len(BootPeers) /\ e.target=BootPeers[e.index]
Zeroed(e) == IF e.id \in CancelChanges THEN [e EXCEPT !.target=0, !.changes=[k \in DOMAIN e.changes |-> [e.changes[k] EXCEPT !.target=0]]] ELSE e   \* README:120 NodeID-zero cancellation
ELSE IF t \in c.learners THEN c
ELSE IF t \in c.out THEN [c EXCEPT !.in=@\{t}, !.next=@\cup{t}]
ApplyChanges(c,chs) == IF chs=<<>> THEN c ELSE ApplyChanges(ApplyOne(c,Head(chs)),Tail(chs))
IF Joint(c) \/ c.in={} \/ r.in={} THEN [ok |-> FALSE, cfg |-> c]
IF Joint(c) \/ r.in={} \/ Cardinality((c.in\r.in)\cup(r.in\c.in))>1 THEN [ok |-> FALSE, cfg |-> c]
ConfigOf2(h) == IF h=<<>> THEN EmptyCfg ELSE LET c==ConfigOf2(Prefix(h,Len(h)-1)) e==h[Len(h)] IN
IF e.kind \in ConfKinds2 THEN ConfStep2(c,Zeroed(e)).cfg ELSE c

entries.name: ElectionSafety
entries.proposed: \A a,b \in history.wins: a.term=b.term => a.node=b.node   (verbatim)
entries.control_witness: Shows the effect of defect D3. The bootstrap config is {s1,s2,s3}. A committed EnterJoint(Remove s2, Remove s3, AddVoter s4) yields in={s1,s4}, out={s1,s2,s3}. s4 restores a snapshot taken in that joint config, and source restore (raft.go:1416-1423) keeps only in={s1,s4}. s2 still runs {s1,s2,s3} because it has not applied the V2 entry, and V2 entries do not block Hup (D2). In term T, s1 votes for s4 and s3 votes for s2, so wins={[T,s4],[T,s2]}. This must be flagged. Do not weaken it to per-config uniqueness.

entries.name: LeaderCompleteness

The migrated observer records obligation [2,P], so a later win whose hist does not cover P must be flagged. The unmigrated union observer never records P and misses the violation.

The old ConfigOf ignores this kind of AddLearner, so the old property flags a correct state; ConfigOf2 accepts it. (b) D3. Restore of snapshot s with s.config=[in {s1,s4}, out {s1,s2,s3}, autoLeave TRUE] yields config [in {s1,s4}, out {}] while cfgHist=s.hist. The proposed property flags this. The old union-voters form cannot represent out, next or autoLeave.

entries.name: ConfigurationTransitionSafety
entries.change: representation (full joint config compare; bootstrap exemption made explicit)
evidence: new/source/raft.go:561-581 raft-generated LeaveJoint entries also carry no request id
entries.proposed: \A c \in history.commitUses: \A k \in (c.oldCommit+1)..Len(c.hist): (c.hist[k].kind \in ConfKinds2 /\ ~IsBootstrapEntry(c.hist[k])) => (c.config.in=ConfigOf2(Prefix(c.hist,k-1)).in /\ c.config.out=ConfigOf2(Prefix(c.hist,k-1)).out)   [commitUses records config |-> r.config instead of voters]
entries.disagreement: D1 trace: leader s1's log is [..., J=EnterJoint(Auto), N, L1, L2], where L1 and L2 are raft-generated LeaveJoint entries (id 0). A single MaybeCommit commits L1 and L2 with c.config joint. For k=L2, ConfigOf2(Prefix(hist,L2-1)) is non-joint because L1 has already left, so the proposed property flags it. The old property exempts every id=0 entry and compares only union voters, so it passes.

entries.name: LearnerEligibility

After LeaveJoint s3 is in learners; a grant then must be flagged. A false edit that treats learners ∪ next as learners would flag the first case.

entries.name: QuorumAccounting
entries.change: semantic (quorum definition extended to joint configurations)

entries.disagreement: (a) Starting from {s1,s2,s3}, EnterJoint(Remove s1, AddVoter s4) gives in={s2,s3,s4}, out={s1,s2,s3}. A win by s2 with yes={s2,s3} is a valid joint win, but the old Won over the union {s1..s4} needs 3 votes, so the old property flags a correct election. (b) With in={s1,s4} and out={s1,s2,s3}, yes={s1,s2,s3} is a union majority, so the old property passes. The incoming half lacks a majority, so the proposed property flags it.

The new source demotes, so the old property flags correct behaviour. (b) Removing the last voter: before in={s1}, e=Remove(s1). Old expects voters={}; new expects a fatal error with the config unchanged. (c) Applying a raft-generated LeaveJoint (id 0): the old id=0 clause requires a bootstrap AddVoter and flags it; the new clause accepts it if before is joint. (d) Removing an unknown s4 with CancelUnknownRemovals=FALSE: the old model goes fatal, while the new expectation is a no-op with no fatal.

With in={s1,s4}, out={s1,s2,s3} and the commit durable on {s1,s2,s3}: the union observer records an obligation that the protocol never guaranteed (a spurious alarm).

entries.name: Ghost/observation records (wins, commitUses, EffectObservation, ack records, Campaign/Transfer/Vote/Proposal observations, ReadRecord)

Ack records add role, term, config, pendingBefore and pendingAfter. learner fields stay r.id \in config.learners. Singleton uses Singleton(cfg). No observer may read a value that a protocol guard consumes as its own justification (pendingConf is read only by PendingConfCoverage, against the log).

covered_updated_behaviors.explanation: The Restore and RestartCore ghosts set cfgHist to the snapshot/app prefix while the faithful model takes config from Nodes+Learners only. ConfigOf2(cfgHist) is joint and config is not, so the state invariant fails. Split-brain is the downstream symptom, caught by ElectionSafety, CommittedHistory and AppliedAgreement (kept).

suspected_defects.summary: Auto-leave appends an empty ConfChangeV2 without updating pendingConfIndex. Any later Advance with cursor>=pendingConfIndex, made while the first LeaveJoint is unapplied, appends another one. Applying the second panics cluster-wide ('can't leave a non-joint config'). The same gap lets user conf changes be admitted while the LeaveJoint is pending. Auto-leave also bypasses the leadTransferee drop and does not broadcast.
evidence: new/source/rawnode_test.go:316 asserts the un-bumped value (test pins the defect)
suspected_defects.witness: 3 voters with MaxMsgSize=1 or pagination. The leader appends J=EnterJoint(Auto) at 5 and then a Normal N at 6. Index 5 commits, the app applies J, and Advance appends L1 at 7. Index 6 commits, the next Ready contains [6], and Advance (cursor 6 >= 5 with AutoLeave still TRUE) appends L2 at 8. Applying L2 is fatal. A single-node variant needs MaxReadySize pagination so that a Ready holds [N] alone.
suspected_defects.must_not_be_hidden_by: Dropping PendingConfCoverage because rawnode_test pins the current value; widening the id=0 exemption in ConfigurationTransitionSafety; letting AckPreservation accept multiple appends.

suspected_defects.summary: numOfPendingConf counts only EntryConfChange, so a node with a committed-but-unapplied EntryConfChangeV2 may campaign. stepLeader treats both types as configuration changes, so the two are inconsistent. Election safety alone is preserved by joint-quorum overlap, but the eligibility contract is violated, and together with D3 the violation becomes a split-brain.
suspected_defects.must_not_be_hidden_by: Restricting the pending scan to V1 kinds.

suspected_defects.summary: restore() and newRaft(InitialState) rebuild the config from ConfState.Nodes and .Learners only, dropping NodesJoint, LearnersNext and AutoLeave. A node restored or restarted inside a joint config runs a non-joint config, decides elections and commits on the incoming half only, and never auto-leaves. The restore membership check also ignores NodesJoint, so an outgoing-only voter rejects every snapshot (a liveness problem).
suspected_defects.witness: See the ElectionSafety control witness: two leaders in term T in a 4-server model.
suspected_defects.must_not_be_hidden_by: Comparing only config.in in ConfigurationOrigin, or idealising Restore/RestartCore in the model.

suspected_defects.summary: Conf-change admission uses raft's applied index. With early Advance (README:122), raft.applied can pass a committed EnterJoint before the app calls ApplyConfChange. A user conf change is then admitted against what looks like a non-joint config and later fails when applied in the joint config ('can't apply simple config change in joint config' or 'config is already joint'). In the old code the two pending simple changes composed safely.
suspected_defects.witness: EarlyAdvance=TRUE. J=EnterJoint commits; Ready and QueueApplication run; Advance sets applied=J while the app has not yet applied J. Propose V1 AddLearner(s4) is admitted at J+1. The app applies J (joint). J+1 commits and the app applies it: Fatal.
suspected_defects.must_not_be_hidden_by: Treating EffectContract2's fatal branch as acceptance. That branch describes the effect function, not whether the fatal is acceptable.

suspected_defects.summary: Changer.Simple returns (empty Config, empty ProgressMap, nil error) when checkInvariants fails, so it silently wipes the config instead of returning an error. It is believed unreachable because apply() preserves the invariants.
Config.Clone omits AutoLeave, so Status().Config.AutoLeave is always false. There is no protocol impact, because Changer paths reset or forbid AutoLeave.

StartNode ignores Bootstrap's error, so a non-empty storage silently skips bootstrap. README:83 still tells callers to start a joining node with StartNode and an empty peer list, which now panics. README and doc.go describe applying only EntryConfChange, never EntryConfChangeV2, although raft now emits V2 entries itself.

RawNode.Ready is read-only and Advance runs acceptReady, which clears msgs and readStates and sets prevSoftSt. Any Step between Ready and Advance therefore loses messages and read states. The doc now forbids this, but the current model allows it.
Promoting a learner to voter no longer sets RecentActive (the old code did, raft.go:1432-1435). A freshly promoted voter can count as inactive at the next CheckQuorum and make the leader step down.

These model parts must be migrated faithfully to the source, including its defects, or the witnesses above become unreachable: ApplyConfCore ('remove unknown peer' fatal, CancelUnknownRemovals, active:=TRUE on promotion, maybeCommit only on Remove); InitialRaft/RestartCore (joining term 1, the RawNode 'fresh' term-1 bump, Node prevHS=EmptyHS on restart); ProtocolReady clearing out and quota for RawNodes; QuorumIndex, vote tally, StepCheckQuorum, ReadOnlyRecvAck and read singleton using a single voter set; StepHup scan; Restore; WrapperLoop proposal gating.
